title: IPO・マーケット監視ボード

items.title:
Anthropic has filed for an IPO, with its prospectus revealing just how fast the company is scaling.
FY25 revenue jumped 1,088% YoY to $4.59B, while compute and infrastructure spending rose 190% to $7.33B.
The company posted an $8.06B operating loss and ended 2025 with $20.28B in cash and short-term investments.
Anthropic’s two largest direct customers accounted for 24% of total revenue combined.
items.title_ja:
Anthropic は IPO を申請しており、その目論見書により同社がいかに急速に拡大しているかが明らかになりました。
25 年度の収益は前年比 1,088% 増の 45 億 9000 万ドルとなり、コンピューティングとインフラストラクチャへの支出は 190% 増の 73 億 3000 万ドルとなりました。
同社は80億6000万ドルの営業損失を計上し、2025年終了時点では202億8000万ドルの現金と短期投資を残した。
Anthropic の 2 つの最大の直接顧客は、合計収益の 24% を占めました。

items.title:
Rogo, an AI startup for Wall Street founded by former junior bankers, has jumped to a $3.75 billion valuation, Bloomberg News reports.
Rogo raised $160 million in April in a Series D led by Kleiner Perkins, with Sequoia, Thrive Capital and J.P. Morgan also backing the company.
items.title_ja:
ブルームバーグニュースの報道によると、元若手銀行員らが設立したウォール街のAIスタートアップ、ロゴの評価額は37億5000万ドルに跳ね上がった。
ロゴは4月にクライナー・パーキンス氏率いるシリーズDで1億6000万ドルを調達し、セコイア、スライブ・キャピタル、JPモルガンも同社を支援した。

items.title:
EasyPost, whose shipping software customers include Amazon and FedEx, will go public on Nasdaq through a merger with the SPAC American Drive Acquisition at a $576 million enterprise value.
It expects 2026 revenue of $141 million, up 31%, and will trade as EZPO.
items.title_ja:
AmazonやFedExなどの配送ソフトウェア顧客を持つEasyPostは、SPAC American Drive Acquisitionとの合併を通じて5億7,600万ドルの企業価値でナスダックに上場する予定だ。
2026年の収益は31%増の1億4,100万ドルになると予想しており、EZPOとして取引される予定だ。

items.title:
EQT is considering selling Indira IVF, India's biggest IVF chain, and may seek a valuation of at least $1.5 billion, Bloomberg News reports.
Indira filed confidentially for an Indian IPO in July 2025 that was expected to raise about $408 million.
items.title_ja:
EQTはインド最大の体外受精チェーンであるインディラIVFの売却を検討しており、少なくとも15億ドルの評価額を求める可能性があるとブルームバーグニュースが報じた。
インディラは2025年7月にインドでのIPOを極秘に申請し、約4億800万ドルの調達が見込まれていた。

items.title:
KKR and Carlyle are investing $475 million in Litmus Music, the Wall Street Journal reports.
KKR comes in as a minority investor while Carlyle keeps its majority stake in the music-rights company, which struck a deal for the rights to five Katy Perry albums in 2023.
items.title_ja:
KKRとカーライルはリトマス・ミュージックに4億7,500万ドルを投資しているとウォール・ストリート・ジャーナルが報じた。
KKRは少数投資家として参加する一方、カーライルは音楽著作権会社の過半数株を維持し、2023年にケイティ・ペリーのアルバム5枚の権利に関する契約を結んだ。

items.title:
Payhawk raised $280 million in a Series C round led by Goldman Sachs Alternatives' growth equity team, valuing the spend-management startup at $2 billion, the company said.
That doubles the $1 billion valuation Payhawk reached in 2022. Founded in Sofia, Bulgaria, the company operates in 33 countries and has raised more than $515 million in total. Existing backers including QED, Greenoaks and Lightspeed also invested.
items.title_ja:
Payhawkは、Goldman Sachs Alternativesのグロース・エクイティ・チームが主導するシリーズCラウンドで2億8,000万ドルを調達し、支出管理スタートアップの評価額を20億ドルと同社は述べた。
これは、ペイホークが2022年に達成した評価額10億ドルの2倍となる。同社はブルガリアのソフィアで設立され、33カ国で事業を展開し、総額5億1,500万ドル以上を調達した。 QED、Greenoaks、Lightspeedなどの既存の支援者も投資した。

items.title:
METKA, the infrastructure and engineering unit of Greece's Metlen Energy & Metals, set a price range of €10.00 to €11.50 per share for its Euronext Athens IPO, the company said.
The range implies a market value of about €1.25 billion to €1.40 billion after the offering, and the deal could total about €350 million to €365 million including an upsize option, according to a bookrunner. Metlen will keep control. Books close Nov. 20, with trading set to begin Nov. 26.
items.title_ja:
ギリシャのメトレン・エナジー・アンド・メタルズのインフラ・エンジニアリング部門であるMETKAは、ユーロネクスト・アテネIPOの価格範囲を1株当たり10.00ユーロから11.50ユーロに設定したと同社は述べた。
ブックランナーによれば、この範囲は公募後の市場価値が約12億5000万ユーロから14億ユーロになることを意味しており、契約は大型オプションを含めると総額約3億5000万ユーロから3億6500万ユーロになる可能性があるという。メトレンが主導権を握るだろう。帳簿は11月20日に締め切り、取引は11月26日に開始される予定。

items.title:
Bets on Anthropic's shares in crypto markets imply a valuation of about $1.7 trillion ahead of its IPO, despite the recent slump in AI stocks, Bloomberg reports.
That is above the $1.5 trillion to $1.6 trillion the IPO could value Anthropic at if shares price above $80, as The Wall Street Journal reported. Pricing is expected Wednesday, with trading set to start Thursday.
items.title_ja:
ブルームバーグの報道によると、最近のAI株の低迷にもかかわらず、暗号通貨市場でのアンスロピック株への賭けは、IPOに先立って約1兆7000億ドルの評価額が予想されることを意味している。
これは、ウォール・ストリート・ジャーナルが報じたように、株価が80ドルを超えた場合にIPOでアンスロピック社の評価額が予想される1兆5000億〜1兆6000億ドルを上回っている。価格決定は水曜日に予想され、取引は木曜日に開始される予定だ。

items.title:
SoftBank founder Masayoshi Son said passing up an earlier chance to invest in Anthropic was one of his "mistakes," Nikkei Asia reports.
Speaking at a Nikkei forum in Tokyo on Wednesday, Son also said the real show for AI is only beginning. SoftBank is one of OpenAI's largest backers, and Anthropic is set to price its IPO this week.
items.title_ja:
ソフトバンク創業者の孫正義氏は、アンスロピックへの投資チャンスを早期に逃したことは「間違い」の一つだったと日経アジアが報じた。
孫氏は水曜日、東京で開催された日経フォーラムで講演し、AIの本当の勝負はまだ始まったばかりだとも語った。ソフトバンクはOpenAIの最大の支援者の1つであり、Anthropicは今週IPOの価格を決定する予定だ。

items.title:
A consortium of Qatari investors plans to fully exit its stake in Ennismore, the lifestyle hotel group behind The Hoxton, Mondrian and Mama Shelter, as Accor buys out the company's minority shareholders, Lesha Bank said.
The deals value Ennismore's equity at about €3.7 billion, around 18 times estimated 2027 EV/EBITDA. Accor plans to buy 44.3% of Ennismore in stages through January 2028 for about €1.6 billion and is still weighing strategic partners or a public listing for the business.
items.title_ja:
レシャ銀行によると、アコーが同社の少数株主を買収するのに伴い、カタールの投資家連合は、ホクストン、モンドリアン、ママ・シェルターを運営するライフスタイルホテルグループ、エニスモアへの株式を完全に手放す計画だという。
この取引により、エニズモアの株式価値は約37億ユーロとなり、2027年の推定EV/EBITDAの約18倍となる。アコーは２０２８年１月まで段階的にエニズモア株の４４．３％を約１６億ユーロで買収する計画で、戦略的パートナーや同事業の上場を検討中だ。

items.title:
Selling stockholders in Medline $MDLN priced a secondary offering of 60 million Class A shares at $35.50 each, about $2.13 billion, the company said.
The price is 5.8% below Tuesday's $37.68 close and 22% above the $29 IPO price from December 2025, when Medline raised $6.26 billion in 2025's biggest IPO. The shares fell 4.5% in the two sessions after the deal was launched. Medline receives no proceeds.
items.title_ja:
同社によると、メドライン$MDLNの株主への売却により、クラスA株6000万株の売出価格は1株当たり35.50ドル、約21億3000万ドルとなったという。
この価格は火曜日の終値37.68ドルを5.8％下回り、メドラインが2025年最大のIPOで62億6000万ドルを調達した2025年12月のIPO価格29ドルを22％上回っている。取引開始後の２セッションで株価は４．５％下落した。 Medline は収益を受け取りません。

items.title:
Anthropic backers including Sequoia Capital, Lightspeed Venture Partners and Iconiq plan to buy billions of dollars' worth of shares in the AI company's IPO, according to Bloomberg.
Anthropic's order book closed at 4pm New York time on Tuesday, and the company now expects to price its shares above $80, above its marketed $70 to $78 range, The Wall Street Journal reported.
items.title_ja:
ブルームバーグによると、セコイア・キャピタル、ライトスピード・ベンチャー・パートナーズ、アイコニックなどの人類支援者らは、AI企業のIPOで数十億ドル相当の株式を購入する計画だという。
アンスロピックの注文帳は火曜日のニューヨーク時間午後４時に終了し、同社は現在、同社株の価格が市場市場の70ドルから78ドルの範囲を上回る80ドルを超えると予想しているとウォール・ストリート・ジャーナル紙が報じた。

items.title:
AMPERA, a next-generation energy company building modular power systems for AI data centers and defense, is going public through a merger with blank-check firm Berto Acquisition Corp $TACO at a $900 million pre-money equity value, the companies said Tuesday.
The deal could raise up to $357 million, including $317 million held in Berto's trust assuming no redemptions and a PIPE of more than $30 million. AMPERA plans near-term power generation from heat recovery and conventional fuels while developing advanced nuclear technology.
The combined company is expected to list on Nasdaq as AMPR, with the deal targeted to close in the first quarter of 2027.
items.title_ja:
AIデータセンターや防衛用のモジュラー電源システムを構築する次世代エネルギー会社AMPERAが、白紙小切手会社Berto Acquisition Corp $TACOとの合併を通じてプレマネーの株式価値9億ドルで株式を公開すると両社が火曜日に発表した。
この取引により、償還なしと仮定したベルト氏の信託で保有される3億1,700万ドルと3,000万ドルを超えるPIPEを含め、最大3億5,700万ドルが調達される可能性がある。 AMPERA は、先進的な原子力技術を開発しながら、熱回収と従来型燃料による短期的な発電を計画しています。
合併後の会社はAMPRとしてナスダックに上場する予定で、取引は2027年の第1四半期に完了する予定だ。

items.title:
Mistral AI is getting ready to go public and will most likely list in Europe, CEO Arthur Mensch said at a Semafor event on Tuesday, though not this year.
"The natural place to list is Europe," Mensch said. The French AI company raised €3 billion in a Series D led by Samsung in September at a valuation of more than €21 billion, about $24 billion.
items.title_ja:
ミストラルAIは株式公開の準備を進めており、年内には上場しないものの、火曜日のセマフォーのイベントで最高経営責任者（CEO）アーサー・メンシュ氏は欧州で上場する可能性が高いと述べた。
「リストに挙げるのが自然な場所はヨーロッパだ」とメンシュ氏は語った。フランスのAI企業は9月にサムスン主導のシリーズDで30億ユーロを調達し、評価額は210億ユーロ以上（約240億ドル）となった。

items.title:
Corporate card startup Ramp is in early talks with investors to raise $1 billion or more at a $70 billion valuation, according to The Wall Street Journal.
It would be Ramp's third fundraise in a year. The company was valued at $60 billion in October, when it raised $1.85 billion in a round led by Dragoneer and said annualized revenue had passed $2 billion. It was valued at $44 billion in June.
items.title_ja:
ウォール・ストリート・ジャーナルによると、法人カードの新興企業ランプは、700億ドルの評価額で10億ドル以上を調達するために投資家と初期の交渉を行っているという。
ランプ氏にとってこの1年で3回目の資金調達となる。ドラゴニア主導のラウンドで18億5000万ドルを調達した10月時点では同社の評価額は600億ドルと評価され、年間収益は20億ドルを超えたと発表した。 6月時点では440億ドルと評価されていた。

大企業向け統合人事システム「COMPANY」を手がけるWHIホールディングスが、東証プライム市場への上場承認を受けました。上場日は12月15日です。
想定仮条件は2,340〜2,590円で、平均の2,465円で計算すると時価総額は約3,813億円。
2026年のIPOでは時価総額、調達規模ともに最大の案件です。
新株の発行はなく、既存株主による売り出しのみです。売出株数はオーバーアロットメントを含めると約4,915万株、約1,211億円になります。
グローバル・オファリングで、主幹事は野村證券、SMBC日興証券、BofA証券、ゴールドマン・サックス証券です。
前身のワークスアプリケーションズが次世代製品「HUE」の開発失敗と顧客との訴訟で経営難に陥り、2019年8月に会社分割で切り出したHR事業をベインキャピタルが取得しました。取得額は約1,000億円とみられています。
2023年7月、ベインは新ファンドから再出資し、シンガポール政府系ファンドのGICとの共同保有に移行しました。
その後、2024年にサイダスを約66億円、2025年にエンバーポイントを約228億円で取得しました。エンバーポイントはベイン傘下からの取得です。現在の保有比率は、完全希薄化ベースでベイン56.78%、GIC39.88%です。
2025年12月期は、売上収益657億円（前期比21.9%増）、調整後EBITDAは305億円（同27.2%増）で、マージンは46%でした。2026年1〜9月期は、売上収益562億円（同18.0%増）、調整後EBITDA291億円（同23.0%増）で、マージンは52%まで上がっています。
一方、最終損益は1〜9月期で赤字です。借り換えに伴う手数料の一括費用化や、合併で税務上の繰越欠損金を一部引き継げなかったことが響きました。
顧客基盤の強さは際立っています。
・導入先：約1,200法人グループ
・年間解約率：1.0%
・NRR：112%
・契約10年以上の顧客：66%
・クラウド比率：2021年末の16.8%から2026年9月末に81.5%
大企業の給与計算は一度入れると替えにくく、クラウド移行による単価アップを着実に取り込んでいます。
2023年の再出資時の株主資本は約1,547億円、1株1,000円です。想定価格2,465円なら株式ベースで約2.5倍、約3.4年のIRRで30%前後と試算できます。
純有利子負債は約1,750億円で、時価総額に足した企業価値は約5,560億円で、直近12カ月の調整後EBITDA約359億円に対するEV/EBITDAは約15.5倍です。10月に報じられた「企業価値ベースで5,000億円超」になっています
ただし、今回売却するのは保有株の3割程度にとどまり、上場後もファンドが約3分の2を保有し続ける計算です。
リターンの大半は上場後の株価次第で、残りを段階的に売っていく形になります。
2019年取得分のベイン旧ファンドは、企業価値ベースで約1,000億円から約3,500億円へ約3.5倍にしていて、レバレッジを考えると、株式ベースのリターンはそれ以上です。
破綻寸前の会社から最も価値のある事業を切り出し、7年で2度のLBOとボルトオン買収（周辺企業の追加買収）を重ねて上場させる。日本のPEカーブアウト案件のお手本のような案件ですね。

11月12日、フォースタートアップスの社員の皆さんに向けて講演しました。Q＆Aセッションでは、ある社員から、社員の採用や抜擢で何を見ているのかと聞かれ、事業を任せる人については「熱狂しているかどうか」で選ぶと答えました。市場成長性が高く、市場で首位を狙える事業アイディアでも、推進者が熱狂していなければうまくいかないと考えているからです。
例に挙げたのは、弁護士ドットコムが提供する法律分野の生成AI、LegalBrain エージェントの立ち上げです。
LegalBrainを構想した2023年当時、この構想は私の頭の中にあるだけで、プロダクト開発の推進者はいませんでした。プロダクト開発を推進するPdMを採用する面接では多くの候補者に会い、私の構想に熱狂してくれるかどうかを最も重視しました。そうして入社したのが、現在、LegalBrain事業本部のHead of Productを務める稲垣でした。LegalBrain事業本部長の鈴木大介、bizDev部長の田村はじめ事業本部のメンバーの実行力や全社の支援協力もあり、結果としてLegalBrain エージェントは成長を重ね、11月には国内上場企業の主要SaaSプロダクトの中で市場最速の17.3カ月でARR10億円に達するまでになりました。
一般的に、上場企業の新規事業は、立ち上げの時期には投資先行するが故に社内から応援されにくく、計画どおりに進むこともまずありません。それでも熱狂している推進者なら、社内の声にとらわれず、壁にぶつかっても折れずに進むことが期待できます。推進者が折れれば、事業はそこで終わります。
フォースタートアップスの社員の皆さんの質問には、大いに刺激を受けました。事業を前に進めるのは、何より推進する人の熱狂です。弁護士ドットコムはこれからも新しい事業に挑戦し続け、そのたびに熱狂している人とともに事業を成長させていきます。

If you own ANY AI stocks, you need to read this.
“Our momentum is real. Our demand is accelerating. Our supply is growing. Our customers and our partners are with us. And employees are committed.” That was how NVIDIA's interim CEO Colette Kress ended what might be one of the most important earnings calls in the company's history. NVIDIA came into this quarter facing some serious concerns. Jensen Huang's departure, circular financing, the sustainability of AI spending, declining margins, export restrictions, and whether the company could continue executing without its founder. And I think management did a pretty good job addressing most of them.
First, the numbers were absolutely incredible. NVIDIA reported $116 billion in quarterly revenue, more than doubling year over year and growing 20% sequentially. Data center revenue reached $108 billion, up 21% quarter over quarter, while Vera Rubin generated nearly $20 billion in its first quarter of production shipments, making it the fastest product ramp in NVIDIA's history. Management also guided for $130 billion in Q4 revenue and raised its fiscal 2028 revenue growth outlook from 70% to 75%. Think about that for a second. We're talking about a company already generating more than $100 billion in quarterly revenue that still expects 75% annual growth in fiscal 2028. One of the biggest concerns was obviously Jensen Huang's departure. Interestingly, Jensen was only mentioned twice by name during the entire call. It almost felt like management wanted to distance the conversation from Jensen and shift investors' attention back to the business. The board explicitly stated that Jensen would not return as CEO and refused to discuss the ongoing investigation. Instead, Colette emphasized that NVIDIA's employees, leadership team, customers, and suppliers remain fully committed. She even mentioned that TSMC's leadership had been in NVIDIA's offices this week. The company also confirmed that Vera Rubin Ultra remains on track for next year, with Feynman expected in 2028. Now, despite the board saying Jensen isn't coming back, I personally still think there's a small chance we could eventually see him return in some capacity. I wouldn't bet on it, but I wouldn't completely rule it out either.
Another major concern was circular financing, particularly NVIDIA's financial relationships with neoclouds and other AI infrastructure companies. Investors have been worried that NVIDIA is essentially financing customers who then purchase its GPUs. Management clarified that many of its guarantees only take effect once customers have secured financing and their infrastructure is ready for deployment. If those conditions aren't met, certain commitments can be reduced or eliminated. Colette also confirmed this wasn't a new policy, just additional disclosure explaining how the arrangements work. That doesn't eliminate the risk, especially with NVIDIA carrying $118 billion in guarantees and $32 billion in neocloud related commitments, but it does provide more transparency. And speaking of neoclouds, I thought this was one of the most bullish parts of the entire call for companies like $NBIS and $CRWV. NVIDIA's AI Cloud, Industrial, and Enterprise segment generated $47 billion in revenue, growing 18% sequentially and nearly tripling year over year. Management emphasized that neoclouds are becoming increasingly important to the AI ecosystem, helping enterprises, governments, and AI labs access computing capacity.
NVIDIA revealed that Hopper GPUs are being recontracted at up to twice their original rental prices, while B300 rental rates have increased more than 60% since introduction. Management also confirmed that its compute remains fully utilized across every hyperscaler and neocloud it serves. That's a pretty big deal because one of the biggest bearish arguments against neoclouds has been that their expensive GPUs would rapidly lose value as newer hardware became available. Instead, we're seeing older GPUs retain significant economic value while newer hardware commands higher rental rates. $NBIS jumped more than 12% following those comments, and I think it's pretty clear why. If these pricing and utilization trends continue, the economics for well positioned neocloud operators could be considerably better than many investors expected. Another concern was whether the AI infrastructure boom was approaching its peak. NVIDIA pushed back with some pretty incredible numbers. Cloud industry backlog increased from $2 trillion to $2.5 trillion in just three months, while hyperscaler cloud revenue growth accelerated for the sixth consecutive quarter. Meanwhile, token volumes on OpenRouter increased 35 times year over year, with AI agents now accounting for approximately 80% of tokens. Token prices have also declined nearly 60% since May, encouraging significantly greater usage. Essentially, AI is becoming cheaper to use, but consumption is growing so quickly that demand for computing infrastructure continues to accelerate.
Margins were another major topic. NVIDIA expects Q4 gross margins to decline to 71%–72%, but management explicitly described that quarter as the bottom, with margins expected to recover to 72%–73% in fiscal 2028. Colette explained that NVIDIA had honored existing purchase orders despite rising supply costs and expects updated pricing to help stabilize margins. That's reassuring considering the concerns around memory costs, advanced packaging, and competition from custom AI chips. Management also addressed supply constraints, confirming that NVIDIA has secured additional memory and advanced packaging capacity. Vera Rubin is being deployed roughly twice as fast as Grace Blackwell, with hyperscalers bringing the platform into production in approximately one month. NVIDIA is also prioritizing customers that have secured financing, sufficient power, and data centers ready to deploy its hardware. That's particularly important because demand means very little if customers can't actually install and operate the infrastructure.
There were also questions about a potential slowdown in 2028 due to political uncertainty, electricity constraints, and opposition to data center construction. Management acknowledged those risks but emphasized that customers are still requesting more supply than NVIDIA can currently deliver. The company also established a National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee to strengthen engagement with the US government. Importantly, its guidance already excludes future licensed Hopper shipments to China, although the latest export restrictions are still being evaluated. Another encouraging development was capital allocation. NVIDIA returned $28 billion to shareholders during the quarter, including $22 billion in buybacks and $6 billion in dividends. It also increased its repurchase authorization by $150 billion, leaving $227 billion available at quarter-end. Management intends to execute that authorization by the end of fiscal 2028 while continuing to invest in supply chain expansion and selected infrastructure partnerships.
Overall, I think NVIDIA delivered exactly the kind of earnings call investors needed following the uncertainty of the past week. Management addressed nearly every major concern, raised its long-term growth outlook, and showed that demand for AI infrastructure remains exceptionally strong. Of course, Jensen's departure is still a major uncertainty, circular financing risks haven't completely disappeared, and customers will eventually need to demonstrate sufficient returns on their enormous AI investments. But when you have a company generating $116 billion in quarterly revenue, guiding for $130 billion next quarter, and still expecting 75% revenue growth in fiscal 2028, it's pretty difficult to argue that the underlying business is falling apart. Whether that's enough to reverse the recent stock decline remains to be seen, but I think NVIDIA gave the bulls plenty of ammunition tonight.

Jensen Huang might actually be making a comeback to NVIDIA and things are getting pretty interesting behind the scenes.
According to a new exclusive report from Semafor, some NVIDIA board members are continuing to push for Jensen Huang to return as CEO, despite the company publicly stating that it has no plans to bring him back. Apparently, there's a faction within the board that believes reinstating Jensen would be the right decision, which suggests the board might not be as united as NVIDIA wants investors to believe. Jensen himself has already said he would be honored to return if the board decided it was in NVIDIA's best interests. So the biggest obstacle right now isn't necessarily Jensen's willingness to come back, but rather whether the directors opposing his return can be convinced to change their minds.
Meanwhile, NVIDIA is reportedly considering other candidates, including Arm CEO Rene Haas and Marvell CEO Matt Murphy. However, Haas reportedly has concerns about taking the job while there's still a public campaign to bring Jensen back. And honestly, I can't blame him. Imagine becoming CEO of NVIDIA while half the industry is calling for your predecessor to return. Another interesting detail is that Jensen still owns roughly 3.5% of NVIDIA, which could potentially give him some influence over the board through shareholder voting mechanisms. That doesn't guarantee anything, but it means he's not entirely powerless in this situation.
Personally, I think bringing Jensen back would be a massive positive for NVIDIA, especially given everything that's happened over the past week. The company just delivered incredible earnings, but there are still questions surrounding its leadership, the ongoing investigations, and whether it can maintain the same execution without the person who helped build it into what it is today. I'm not saying Jensen is definitely coming back, especially with the investigations still hanging over everything, but I think the possibility is becoming harder to dismiss. And if more directors start supporting his return, things could change pretty quickly.
Melvin (@MelvinInvests)
If you own ANY AI stocks, you need to read this.
“Our momentum is real. Our demand is accelerating. Our supply is growing. Our customers and our partners are with us. And employees are committed.” That was how NVIDIA's interim CEO Colette Kress ended what might be one of the most important earnings calls in the company's history. NVIDIA came into this quarter facing some serious concerns. Jensen Huang's departure, circular financing, the sustainability of AI spending, declining margins, export restrictions, and whether the company could continue executing without its founder. And I think management did a pretty good job addressing most of them.
First, the numbers were absolutely incredible. NVIDIA reported $116 billion in quarterly revenue, more than doubling year over year and growing 20% sequentially. Data center revenue reached $108 billion, up 21% quarter over quarter, while Vera Rubin generated nearly $20 billion in its first quarter of production shipments, making it the fastest product ramp in NVIDIA's history. Management also guided for $130 billion in Q4 revenue and raised its fiscal 2028 revenue growth outlook from 70% to 75%. Think about that for a second. We're talking about a company already generating more than $100 billion in quarterly revenue that still expects 75% annual growth in fiscal 2028. One of the biggest concerns was obviously Jensen Huang's departure. Interestingly, Jensen was only mentioned twice by name during the entire call. It almost felt like management wanted to distance the conversation from Jensen and shift investors' attention back to the business. The board explicitly stated that Jensen would not return as CEO and refused to discuss the ongoing investigation. Instead, Colette emphasized that NVIDIA's employees, leadership team, customers, and suppliers remain fully committed. She even mentioned that TSMC's leadership had been in NVIDIA's offices this week. The company also confirmed that Vera Rubin Ultra remains on track for next year, with Feynman expected in 2028. Now, despite the board saying Jensen isn't coming back, I personally still think there's a small chance we could eventually see him return in some capacity. I wouldn't bet on it, but I wouldn't completely rule it out either.
Another major concern was circular financing, particularly NVIDIA's financial relationships with neoclouds and other AI infrastructure companies. Investors have been worried that NVIDIA is essentially financing customers who then purchase its GPUs. Management clarified that many of its guarantees only take effect once customers have secured financing and their infrastructure is ready for deployment. If those conditions aren't met, certain commitments can be reduced or eliminated. Colette also confirmed this wasn't a new policy, just additional disclosure explaining how the arrangements work. That doesn't eliminate the risk, especially with NVIDIA carrying $118 billion in guarantees and $32 billion in neocloud related commitments, but it does provide more transparency. And speaking of neoclouds, I thought this was one of the most bullish parts of the entire call for companies like $NBIS and $CRWV. NVIDIA's AI Cloud, Industrial, and Enterprise segment generated $47 billion in revenue, growing 18% sequentially and nearly tripling year over year. Management emphasized that neoclouds are becoming increasingly important to the AI ecosystem, helping enterprises, governments, and AI labs access computing capacity.
NVIDIA revealed that Hopper GPUs are being recontracted at up to twice their original rental prices, while B300 rental rates have increased more than 60% since introduction. Management also confirmed that its compute remains fully utilized across every hyperscaler and neocloud it serves. That's a pretty big deal because one of the biggest bearish arguments against neoclouds has been that their expensive GPUs would rapidly lose value as newer hardware became available. Instead, we're seeing older GPUs retain significant economic value while newer hardware commands higher rental rates. $NBIS jumped more than 12% following those comments, and I think it's pretty clear why. If these pricing and utilization trends continue, the economics for well positioned neocloud operators could be considerably better than many investors expected. Another concern was whether the AI infrastructure boom was approaching its peak. NVIDIA pushed back with some pretty incredible numbers. Cloud industry backlog increased from $2 trillion to $2.5 trillion in just three months, while hyperscaler cloud revenue growth accelerated for the sixth consecutive quarter. Meanwhile, token volumes on OpenRouter increased 35 times year over year, with AI agents now accounting for approximately 80% of tokens. Token prices have also declined nearly 60% since May, encouraging significantly greater usage. Essentially, AI is becoming cheaper to use, but consumption is growing so quickly that demand for computing infrastructure continues to accelerate.
Margins were another major topic. NVIDIA expects Q4 gross margins to decline to 71%–72%, but management explicitly described that quarter as the bottom, with margins expected to recover to 72%–73% in fiscal 2028. Colette explained that NVIDIA had honored existing purchase orders despite rising supply costs and expects updated pricing to help stabilize margins. That's reassuring considering the concerns around memory costs, advanced packaging, and competition from custom AI chips. Management also addressed supply constraints, confirming that NVIDIA has secured additional memory and advanced packaging capacity. Vera Rubin is being deployed roughly twice as fast as Grace Blackwell, with hyperscalers bringing the platform into production in approximately one month. NVIDIA is also prioritizing customers that have secured financing, sufficient power, and data centers ready to deploy its hardware. That's particularly important because demand means very little if customers can't actually install and operate the infrastructure.
There were also questions about a potential slowdown in 2028 due to political uncertainty, electricity constraints, and opposition to data center construction. Management acknowledged those risks but emphasized that customers are still requesting more supply than NVIDIA can currently deliver. The company also established a National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee to strengthen engagement with the US government. Importantly, its guidance already excludes future licensed Hopper shipments to China, although the latest export restrictions are still being evaluated. Another encouraging development was capital allocation. NVIDIA returned $28 billion to shareholders during the quarter, including $22 billion in buybacks and $6 billion in dividends. It also increased its repurchase authorization by $150 billion, leaving $227 billion available at quarter-end. Management intends to execute that authorization by the end of fiscal 2028 while continuing to invest in supply chain expansion and selected infrastructure partnerships.

On market crashes like today, I'm reminded of a piece of advice I got from a CIO mentor that traded during the dotcom and 08 crashes and lived to tell the tale.
He said: "Treat investing the same way you treat life."
That's all. It has stuck with me for many years because after filling in the blanks, you're forced to become "better" in both portfolio management and life management. It's uncanny how correlated they are.
Strip either one down and you're left with the same raw materials: time and uncertainty.
Every investment gives up something certain today for something uncertain tomorrow. So does nearly everything that matters in life. Love, learning, raising a child, starting a new job. Anything.
Both reward patience, but only after testing it.
You can't generate performance without risking losses, the same way you can't love without risking grief.
But fundamentally, the first rule of portfolio and life management is survival.
You can come back from most losses, but not from the one that takes you out of the game.
It's always darkest before the dawn.

彼は「人生を扱うのと同じように投資を扱う」と言いました。
それだけです。空白を埋めた後は、ポートフォリオ管理とライフ管理の両方で「より良く」ならざるを得なくなるため、この考えは長年私に引っかかっています。それらがどれほど相関しているかは不思議です。
どちらかを取り除いても、時間と不確実性という同じ原材料が残ります。
すべての投資は、明日の不確実なもののために、今日確実なものを放棄します。人生において重要なことのほぼすべてが同様です。恋愛、学び、子育て、新しい仕事。何でも。
どちらも忍耐に報いますが、それは試した後でのみです。
悲しみのリスクを負わずに愛することができないのと同じように、損失のリスクを負わずにパフォーマンスを生み出すことはできません。
しかし基本的に、ポートフォリオとライフマネジメントの第一のルールは生き残ることです。

Now that we're close to 2027 it's a good idea to stress test downside scenarios where you have:
1. Capex cuts past 2028
2. Stranded Compute / DC Slowdowns
3. Finance deterioration (base case)
4. 2x+ rate hikes
Working in parallel and see what happens with valuations of AI longs.
If you see acceleration despite all 4, I'd argue that's an opportunity.
> Next-gen of photonics is one of the rare segments with an extreme rise in optical content and ASPs that can offset aggregate capex cuts.
Everyone’s moving into that space, including Elon Musk doing M&A, Marvell, Samsung and others with M&A… and we haven’t seen economic impact on emerging architectures even hit players from Celestial to Ayar + their suppliers yet.
If we look at a scenario where there's excess GPUs but power constraints:
We might see slowdown in aggregate accelerator/GPU/ASIC procurement, but your optical engines + light sources + switches players see acceleration.
Especially as incentive to replace power inefficient networking... since different (cheap BOM) optical architectures improves GPU utilization or even HBM requirements.
So value migrates to players more high-beta to architectural shifts.
If Celestial projections are $500m -> $1B, and we expect -30% aggregate capex cuts, I'd argue we'd still see upward revisions from Celestial over the next 2 years.
But financing with #3 matters a lot as seen with $AAOI dropping off of a $550M, vs. $COHR getting prepayments for capacity expansion from their customers.
Companies that rely on external foundries might be less sensitive to #3 since they're not as capex intensive.
On the other hand, companies in sectors have a lot of floating interest like certain Neoclouds, and require further financing might be the most impacted.
> Legacy and specialty memory is a different cycle that markets conflate with AI capex.
If consumer demand weakens but at the same time, players like Windbond exits DDR2, pricing durability is longer than markets expect.
> Wafer/substrate procurement such as ABF, SOI, InP are low cost but large downstream destruction if not secured, so we’ll likely see acceleration here as seen with $NVDA earnings call.
> qualification cycle players within bottlenecks remain very compelling, since first revenue in a large TAM, relative to MC is material to that company.
If a company is valued at $400m then they get a $200m of orders, it's more asymmetrical to a certain company than a rounding error to a $50B incumbent revenue.
_
There’s period of times where prices are dislocated from fundamentals from leveraged players getting wiped. I’d argue that time is now.
I disagree with a lot of the stupid "it's over takes" but I agree it's a good idea to haircut future capex expectations and forward valuations due to financing tightening + macro.
It's also good idea to see the nuances and stress test downside cases.
But TLDR: I'd argue next phase of AI infrastructure is going to be increasingly disconnected from aggregate AI capex growth.
I just personally wrote 4 things I'm using to stress test jointly some of the names I'm looking at, so I'm more comfortable waiting things out... despite seeing hedge funds getting liquidated left and right and overwhelming short positioning.
I personally see acceleration in more narrow parts of the supply chain, while markets treat the entire AI trade as one.
We'll see how things play out on longer horizons.

2027 年が近づいている今、次のような下振れシナリオをストレス テストすることをお勧めします。
1. 2028 年を超えて設備投資を削減
2. コンピューティングの孤立 / DC の速度低下
3. 財務悪化（ベースケース）
4. 2倍以上の利上げ
並行して作業し、AI ロングの評価に何が起こるかを確認します。
4 つすべてにもかかわらず加速が見られる場合、それはチャンスだと私は主張します。
> 次世代フォトニクスは、光学コンテンツと ASP が極端に増加しており、総設備投資削減を相殺できる数少ないセグメントの 1 つです。
M&Aを行っているイーロン・マスク、M&Aを行っているマーベル、サムスンなどを含め、誰もがその分野に移行しつつあります...そして、新興アーキテクチャーへの経済的影響は、CelestialからAyarまでのプレーヤーとそのサプライヤーにさえ及んでいるのはまだ見ていません。
GPU が余っているが電力制約があるシナリオを考えてみると、次のようになります。
アクセラレータ/GPU/ASIC の調達全体では減速が見られるかもしれませんが、光学エンジン + 光源 + スイッチ プレーヤーは加速していると考えられます。
特に、さまざまな (安価な BOM) 光学アーキテクチャにより GPU 使用率が向上し、さらには HBM 要件も改善されるため、電力効率の悪いネットワーキングを置き換えるインセンティブとして役立ちます。

Well, most of the time projections are noise and reactionary.
Like right now, sky-high projections for $ANT $700-$800B ARR over next few years is stirring up hype that I'd argue gets revised down later.
I do think it's important to model in capex forecasts dropping past 2028, due to the current reflexive nature of AI selloffs, rate hikes, etc.
The drawn out duration of Iran War doesn't help, Jensen leaving $NVDA certainty draws concerns over Nvidia's ecosystem.
But any catalyst, like if Iran War ends, can also change sentiment in a heartbeat (since bearish positioning is overwhelming).
- It's also clear financing has been tightening, since OpenAI only managed to raise $11B of their original $30B target so far.
- Markets are reacting enthusiastically to companies like $TE doing a $100M ATM today (nuking valuations)
- Although the "guppy" sector is probably the most sensitive to financing + rate changes.
On bright side... Neoclouds like $NBIS or $IREN seem to be adjusting by getting 100% capex prepayments or 90% GPU prepayments from their counterparties.
What I'd argue though is lower aggregate capex does not apply uniformly in supply chains.
- Mid-high range lasers for NPO/CPO are still sold out, as seen with $LITE now starting negotiations for 2030 capacity.
- MLCCs are seeing further tightening as content usage goes up for AI servers
- ABF substrates to InP substrates not really going anywhere.
If content per system goes up 10X-15X, capacity expands at 2-3X Y/Y, and capex drops 28%.
And content is so cheap that you can triple order and screw over competitors with wafer supply...
I'm pretty confident you'll see acceleration upstream in bottlenecks from optical components to substrates despite potential aggregate capex dropping.
Another rant is:
-I keep seeing this argument that "low P/E is a warning for cyclical that's going to crash" but these are just clown takes
Nobody seems to analyze duration scenarios like capacity expansion vs. content changes vs. demand. to actually see how long those earnings last.
If everyone seems to be exiting DDR2 lines, there's probably going be more tightness in 2027 despite consume demand weakening, even if it looks like it's low P/E.
- Also for concerns about CPO "delays", the same components like lasers are used for NPO. You'll still see 150-200mW NPO lasers or ELS NPO using the same 300–400+ mW lasers as CPO.
We'll just see acceleration with NPO as a bridge if CPO gets delayed and higher range lasers likely to remain in a severe shortage.
- Feels like markets have also completely discredited the merit of take/pay price floor LTAs as well that companies like SK Hynix to Samsung have.
If contractual agreements hold up, memory players look very undervalued.
TLDR:
- I think it's important to model in capex decreasing to numbers like -30% in hypothetical downside sceanrios.
Given AI profitability, it's clearly not sustainable for hyperscalers to aggregately increase capex $500B or $1T+ Y/Y, and that's never been a case I've argued.
- This is also not the same thing as demand destruction that markets are overreacting to now (which haven't happened yet).
- We can see demand revisions for GPUs, ASICs, and heavier cost parts of the supply chain, while acceleration increases elsewhere.
The nuances market miss by indiscriminately selling everything is going to present compelling opportunities when the dust settles. I think in the end institutions are probably going to end up owning more of the same names retail discovered early on.
Anyway, I think it's a good idea to try and survive until more earnings comes out.
Jimbus Last (@JimbusLast)

items.title:
SOME PERSONAL THOUGHTS AHEAD OF WEEKEND
I wanted to share a few thoughts heading into the weekend because at least for me this has been one of most mentally exhausting stretches I've experienced investing in growth stocks.
And honestly one of the things I've found most difficult has very little to do with market itself since it's how much mental real estate I apparently occupy in the minds of certain "gurus" on this platform whom I've never met, followed or even spoken to.
I started sharing my thoughts on X back in 2023 simply because I genuinely love investing and wanted somewhere to talk about market, share my research and connect with people who enjoyed it as much as I did and I never imagined that would turn into an account reaching 100 million impressions every month or that I'd eventually find myself appearing on national television every week.
I'm incredibly grateful because this platform accelerated my career at a relatively young age and opened doors that otherwise might have taken me many more years to reach but I'd be lying if I said spotlight wasn't intense since the larger my audience becomes and more visible I am the more I've realized that success also seems to attract resentment from people I've never interacted with or affected in any way possible.
Daniel has a phrase for this that I think captures it perfectly because "hating up" is absolutely real especially online where people seem more comfortable attacking someone who has become visible than examining why that person's success bothers them in the first place.
Like I've had people accuse me of taking an investment idea from them despite fact that I don't follow them and have never even seen their work while others take a disagreement over a particular thesis and turn it into a personal judgment about whether I know anything about investing.
What I find especially strange is that some of these individuals are in their 40s and 50s have been doing this for decades and still seem determined to tear down a 33 year old who is simply willing to publish his research, explain what he believes and put his own money behind those convictions (I've never asked anyone to agree with me or suggested that my way of investing is the only way to succeed).
And I think that last part is important because I do all of this under my real name and face, publicly disclose what I own through my subs service, share my position sizes and actual dollars I've invested and expose myself to scrutiny over every good decision and every mistake along the way.
There's absolutely nothing wrong with choosing to remain anonymous and I respect anyone who prefers to operate that way but theres just a different level of personal accountability when people know exactly who you are and watch you explain your thesis on camera and follow your positions in real time and wait for first opportunity to use a bad outcome against you... just remember being wrong privately costs you money but being wrong publicly can also cost you reputation, confidence and peace of mind which is something I don't think people fully appreciate until they've experienced it themselves.
None of this is to suggest that criticism should be off limits because disagreement is a huge part of investing but what I truly struggle to understand is why disagreement so often has to become personal... especially during periods like this when so many people are already dealing with painful drawdowns and questioning decisions they made with the best information available to them.
Markets eventually humble every single one of us regardless of how experienced we are or how much success we've had and anyone who stays in this long enough will eventually experience a thesis that breaks or a position they sized too aggressively or a drawdown that exposes a weakness in their process or a decision they wish they could take back so that's why I think showing people grace matters so much because you never know when you'll find yourself on the other side of that experience hoping others will extend you the same understanding.
And also just remember it cost absolutely nothing to root for people, respect the work they're putting in and recognize that someone can be wrong about an investment without deserving to be ridiculed for it and I genuinely wish more people on this platform understood that being publicly wrong doesn't erase courage it takes to stand behind your own convictions in the first place.
And to the people who've made rooting against me a hobby I genuinely hope you find the same energy for your own work that you've found for mine because if you're spending more time waiting for someone else to fail than building something of your own then maybe my portfolio isn't what needs your attention.
I'll be here next week, same name, same face, same conviction.

週末に向けての個人的な考え
少なくとも私にとって、これは成長株への投資で経験した中で最も精神的に疲れる作業の1つだったので、週末に向けていくつかの考えを共有したいと思いました。
そして正直に言うと、私が最も難しいと感じたことの1つは、市場自体とはほとんど関係がありません。それは、私が会ったことも、フォローしたことも、話したことさえない、このプラットフォーム上の特定の「達人」の心の中で私がどれだけの精神的領域を占めていると思われるかということだからです。
私が X についての考えを 2023 年に共有し始めたのは、単純に投資が心から好きで、市場について話したり、自分の研究を共有したり、同じように市場を楽しんでいる人々とつながる場所が欲しかったからです。それが毎月 1 億インプレッションに達するアカウントに成長したり、最終的には全国放送のテレビに毎週出演するようになるとは想像もしていませんでした。
このプラットフォームのおかげで、比較的若い年齢で私のキャリアが加速し、到達するまでにさらに何年もかかっていた可能性がある扉が開かれたので、非常に感謝しています。しかし、視聴者が増えて知名度が上がるほど、成功は、私がこれまで交流したことのない、あるいは何らかの影響を与えたことのない人たちからの怒りを引き寄せるようにも見えることに気づいたので、スポットライトが強くなかったと言ったら嘘になります。
ダニエルはこれについてのフレーズを持っていますが、これはそれを完璧に捉えていると思います。なぜなら、「憎しみ」は絶対に現実のもので、特にオンラインでは、人々は誰かを調べるよりも、目立つようになった人を攻撃する方が安心しているようです。

Here's what Wall Street says about $NVDA after its first earnings since Jensen's exit:
Q3 beat, Q4 guidance topped estimates, FY28 growth raised to 75%, and Jensen's return ruled out.
1. UBS (Buy, $220 PT, cut from $240)
"This should help a little in the near term as some investors have been worried about C2027 cuts, but our view has always been that this is more about how much things decelerate in C2028. On one hand, it would have been nice to see C2028 supply commits increase significantly as well, but on the other hand, we think there is a very real risk that NVDA becomes beholden to these purchase commitments and has to keep throwing money at its customers to drive revenue."
"Lastly, the company announced that the 10-Q will be filed 'in the coming weeks' - later than usual. When queried on our callback, management indicated this was related to the ongoing investigation and whether any additional risk factors would need to be added to the filing."
2. Jefferies (Buy, $250 PT, cut from $300)
"Management noted that cloud industry backlog reached $2.5 trillion, up from $2 trillion three months ago, while Hopper GPUs have recontracted at up to twice their original price and B300 rental rates have increased more than 60% since introduction. In our view, higher rental rates across GPU generations provide tangible evidence that available supply remains well below demand."
"At the same time, we believe the durability of the growth trajectory remains closely linked to spending from leading AI labs and continued evidence of AI ROI, factors largely outside of NVDA’s control."
3. Susquehanna (Positive, $275 PT)
"That said, revenues in the quarter included ~$2.4B of Hopper sales to China that were not previously included in the companys CY3Q guidance. Additionally, there was a 14th week to be included in the fourth quarter."
"To meet its outsized growth expectations, the company increased its supply commitment by roughly ~$110B (now ~$390B), with investments mostly centered on securing additional HBM capacity."
4. Stifel (Buy, $205 PT)
"Three takes for our coverage: (1) NVIDIA’s capital is pivoting from customer financing toward supplier prepayments, positive for substrate, packaging, EMS and optical capacity; (2) networking above $21B with CPO in volume production broadens optical content; and (3) with FY28 growth capped by supply rather than demand, unmet demand creates an opening for second sources."
5. Morgan Stanley (Overweight, $260 PT, cut from $267)
"But given the uncertainty with respect to Commerce Department actions, reports of DOJ and SEC investigations, as well as Nvidia’s own internal investigation related to the CEO transition, we considered it a strong possibility Nvidia would not provide any updates to its prior FY28 guidance."
"However, Nvidia proceeded to raise its guide for FY28 revenue growth from 70% to 75%, and on a higher FY27 base that translates to an incremental $50bn or so in revenues next year vs. the prior outlook."
"We continue to take a more cautious view than management with respect to 2027 revenue growth, raising our estimates from 52% to 56% y/y growth."
6. Truist Securities (Hold, $174 PT)

Mass production of displays for Apple's $AAPL iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 largely won't begin until January, ahead of an expected March 2027 launch.
The reason is that display manufacturers are prioritizing the higher-value iPhone 18 Pro, Pro Max and Duo models through the end of 2026. The standard and Air models require fewer, less complex panels, allowing production to start later.
Apple is also reportedly planning lower production volumes for the iPhone Air 2 following weak demand for the original model.
Samsung is expected to be the sole display supplier for the Air 2, while Samsung and LG Display will split orders for the standard iPhone 18.
Source: AppleInsider

その理由は、ディスプレイメーカーが2026年末まで、より価値の高いiPhone 18 Pro、Pro Max、Duoモデルを優先するためである。標準モデルとAirモデルは必要なパネルが少なく、複雑さが少ないため、生産を後で開始できる。
Appleはまた、オリジナルモデルの需要低迷を受けて、iPhone Air 2の生産量を減らすことを計画していると伝えられている。

items.title:
AMERICA'S TIME ZONES WERE CREATED BY RAILROADS, NOT THE GOVERNMENT
143 years ago today, on Nov. 18, 1883, America's railroads switched the country to standard time.
Before that, every town set its clocks by the sun. Noon in New York was not noon in Philadelphia. For railroads running trains through hundreds of towns, every timetable was a puzzle, and a safety risk.
So the railroads fixed it themselves. They split the country into four zones: Eastern, Central, Mountain and Pacific. At noon on Nov. 18, stations reset their clocks, and in many cities the clocks struck noon twice. It became known as the "Day of Two Noons."
Washington didn't make it law until 1918, when Congress passed the Standard Time Act, 35 years later.
items.title_ja:
アメリカのタイムゾーンは政府ではなく鉄道によって作られた
143 年前の今日、1883 年 11 月 18 日、アメリカの鉄道は国を標準時間に切り替えました。
それまでは、どの町も太陽に合わせて時計を合わせていました。ニューヨークの正午はフィラデルフィアの正午ではありませんでした。何百もの町に列車を走らせる鉄道にとって、時刻表はすべてパズルであり、安全上のリスクでした。
そこで鉄道会社が自ら修理したのです。彼らは国を東部、中部、山岳地帯、太平洋の 4 つのゾーンに分割しました。 11月18日の正午に各駅は時計をリセットし、多くの都市では正午を2回打った。それは「正午二時の日」として知られるようになりました。
ワシントンがこれを法制化したのは、35 年後の 1918 年に議会が標準時法を可決したときでした。

MICKEY MOUSE WAS BORN FROM WALT DISNEY'S WORST BUSINESS SETBACK
98 years ago today, on Nov. 18, 1928, "Steamboat Willie" premiered in New York, marking Mickey Mouse's official public debut.
But Mickey was born out of a business disaster.
Earlier that year, Walt Disney traveled to New York to negotiate a new contract for Oswald the Lucky Rabbit, his first major animated character.
Instead, his distributor, Charles Mintz, wanted to pay him less and had already recruited most of his animators. Worse, Disney discovered that Universal owned the rights to Oswald.
He returned to California without his most successful character and with much of his animation team gone.
Disney later recalled coming up with a new character, a mouse, on the train ride home. Animator Ub Iwerks developed the design, while Walt's wife, Lillian, suggested the name Mickey instead of Mortimer.
But success didn't come immediately.
The first two Mickey cartoons, "Plane Crazy" and "The Gallopin' Gaucho," were silent and failed to secure distribution.
So Disney took another gamble.
Inspired by the arrival of talking pictures, he made a third cartoon with synchronized sound and even supplied Mickey's squeaks himself.
That cartoon was "Steamboat Willie."
It premiered at the Colony Theatre on Broadway, which was leased by Universal, the very studio that owned Oswald.
The audience loved it. Mickey became a hit, and the struggling Disney studio finally had its breakthrough.
The story has an even stranger ending.
Disney didn't regain the rights to Oswald until 2006, when NBCUniversal transferred the character to Disney as part of a deal allowing sportscaster Al Michaels to leave ESPN/ABC for NBC.
And in 2024, the original "Steamboat Willie" entered the U.S. public domain.
Today, Disney is worth roughly $205 billion.
All because Walt lost a character he didn't own and created another one he made sure he did.

ミッキーマウスはウォルト・ディズニーの最悪のビジネス上の挫折から生まれた
98年前の今日、1928年11月18日、『蒸気船ウィリー』がニューヨークで初公開され、ミッキーマウスが正式に公の場にデビューしました。
しかし、ミッキーは経営上の失敗から生まれました。
その年の初め、ウォルト・ディズニーは、彼の最初の主要アニメーションキャラクターであるオズワルド・ザ・ラッキー・ラビットの新たな契約を交渉するためにニューヨークを訪れた。
その代わり、配給会社のチャールズ・ミンツは彼への支払いを減らしたいと考えており、すでにアニメーターのほとんどを採用していた。さらに悪いことに、ディズニーがオズワルドの権利をユニバーサルが所有していることが判明した。
彼は最も成功したキャラクターを失い、アニメーション チームの多くも去ったままカリフォルニアに戻ってきました。
ディズニーは後に、帰りの電車の中で新キャラクターのネズミを思いついたと回想した。アニメーターのウブ・アイワークスがデザインを開発し、ウォルトの妻リリアンがモーティマーではなくミッキーという名前を提案した。
しかし、成功はすぐには訪れませんでした。
最初の 2 つのミッキー漫画「プレーン クレイジー」と「ギャロピン ガウチョ」は沈黙しており、配布を確保することができませんでした。
そこでディズニーは別の賭けに出た。
トーキング・ピクチャーの登場に触発されて、彼は同期サウンドを備えた 3 番目の漫画を作成し、ミッキーの鳴き声も自分で提供しました。
その漫画とは『蒸気船ウィリー』でした。
この作品は、オズワルドを所有していたユニバーサルスタジオが借りていたブロードウェイのコロニー劇場で初演された。
聴衆はそれを気に入りました。ミッキーはヒット作となり、苦境にあったディズニースタジオはついに躍進を遂げた。
物語はさらに奇妙な結末を迎えます。

A majority of Canadians want the country to take in fewer immigrants and temporary residents next year, per Nanos
- Accept fewer: 52.3%
- Keep about the same: 33.5%
- Accept more: 8.4%
- Unsure: 5.9%
It comes after Prime Minister Mark Carney’s government released its 2027–29 plan, which keeps permanent resident targets at 380,000 a year and sets 370,000 new temporary residents a year, and moves up to 348,000 people already in Canada to permanent status.

BREAKING: Nvidia introduced Alibaba to Alice Huang, helping her land the Chinese tech giant as a customer, per The Information.
Nvidia’s sales team introduced Alibaba to Huang on two occasions in 2022, months before US export controls on advanced chips took effect, according to three people with direct knowledge of the matter. Two of them said the introductions helped Huang and her company win Alibaba as a customer.
That deal helped launch her business. Huang was new to chip renting at the time, and with Alibaba on board she was able to get bank loans to finance buying more Nvidia chips, the two people said.
Alice Huang is the suspected Chinese intelligence asset at the center of the scandal that led Jensen Huang to resign as Nvidia CEO.
items.title_ja:
速報: The Information によると、NVIDIA は Alibaba をアリス ファンに紹介し、彼女が中国のテクノロジー大手を顧客として獲得できるよう支援しました。
この件に直接詳しい関係者3人によると、米国の先端チップに対する輸出規制が発効する数カ月前の2022年、NVIDIAの営業チームはアリババをフアン氏に2回紹介したという。そのうちの 2 人は、この紹介がファン氏と彼女の会社がアリババを顧客として獲得するのに役立った、と述べた。
その取引が彼女のビジネスを立ち上げるのに役立った。ファンさんは当時、チップのレンタルに慣れていなかったが、アリババの協力を得て、Nvidiaチップをさらに購入するための資金として銀行融資を受けることができた、と2人は述べた。
アリス・ファンは、ジェンセン・ファンをNVIDIA CEOとして辞任させたスキャンダルの中心人物である中国諜報要員と​​疑われる人物である。

items.title:
US federal debt held by the public has grown bigger than the entire economy, for the first time since World War II, per WaPo.
Debt held by the public reached $31.27 trillion, slightly more than annual US GDP of $31.22 trillion. The previous record was 106% of GDP in 1946.
The Congressional Budget Office projects it will hit 120% by 2036, well above the postwar peak, and interest payments already exceed $1 trillion a year.
items.title_ja:
WaPoによると、国民が保有する米国の連邦債務が第二次世界大戦以来初めて経済全体よりも大きくなった。
国民が抱える借金は31兆2700億ドルに達し、米国の年間GDP31兆2200億ドルをわずかに上回った。これまでの記録は1946年のGDP比106％だった。
議会予算局は、2036年までに戦後のピークを大きく上回る120％に達すると予測しており、利払い費はすでに年間1兆ドルを超えている。
